llm.summary: The skill largely does what it says (TikTok/Douyin analysis + AI generation) and requests the expected API keys, but there are small inconsistencies and a few runtime behaviors (browser automation, process control, unrestricted subprocess patterns) that the user should understand before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description, SKILL.md, manifest, README and code all align: the skill scrapes Douyin data (via TikHub) and calls an AI service (DeepSeek) to generate titles/scripts and stores local ‘memory’. However the top-level registry summary in the provided metadata listed 'Required env vars: none' while manifest.yaml and SKILL.md require TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY — this mismatch is inconsistent and should be clarified.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions only ask to clone and run the included Node script and configure two API keys. The script reads/writes files under scripts/ (scripts/memory/*.json) and may run a headful/headless browser, ffmpeg, whisper, and system commands to manage Xvfb. Those actions are within the described functionality (browser scraping, audio/video processing, local memory). There is no instruction in SKILL.md to read unrelated secrets or to transmit data to unexpected external hosts beyond TikHub/DeepSeek/Douyin.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only + included Node script). No remote download/execute steps were found in the manifest. The script relies on existing system binaries (node, chrome, ffmpeg, whisper, pkill, Xvfb) — reasonable for its browser-automation and media-processing goals but means the host must already provide these tools.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requesting TikHub and DeepSeek API keys is proportionate to the stated purpose. The manifest documents only those two env vars. However the registry summary earlier (requirements: none) contradicts that. Also note: subprocess patterns allow running 'curl *' and other commands; if the platform does not enforce host allowlists for subprocesses, curl could be used to access arbitrary hosts — verify platform-enforced network allowlists are applied.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always: false and the skill does not claim to modify other skills or global agent config. It writes files under its own scripts/memory and config.js (or uses env vars) which is expected. It does require the ability to spawn subprocesses and kill/launch Xvfb processes (pkill/execSync) — normal for browser automation but higher privilege than a pure-API skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement the advertised social-media analysis: it needs two API keys (TikHub and DeepSeek) and will run browser automation (Chromium), media tools (ffmpeg, whisper) and process-control commands (pkill, Xvfb). Before installing: 1) Confirm the manifest’s required env vars (TIKHUB_TOKEN, DEEPSEEK_KEY) with the registry owner — the top-level metadata claiming none is inconsistent. 2) Only provide API keys you trust to these third-party services; avoid using high-privilege or long-lived credentials for unrelated accounts. 3) Run the skill in an isolated environment (container or VM) if you’re uncomfortable with browser automation or pkill usage, since it may start/stop processes and access the network. 4) If you need stricter assurance, review the full marketing_hub.js code (it is included) to verify there are no additional network endpoints or hidden telemetry beyond tikhub / deepseek / douyin. 5) Ensure your OpenClaw/platform enforces subprocess network allowlists so curl/other subprocesses cannot reach arbitrary external hosts.
